thread:
Elaine: quick question about an edge behavior i hit in staging — when client opens a streaming call and we early-ack with 101/upgrade but upstream hasn't accepted yet, we've been reissuing the request on the gateway path. that can create duplicate side-effects if the model infra processed the first one after the gateway retried.

Raj: hmm yeah that's the half-open handshake case. are we talking about the path where frontdoor returns an early 101 and we then later attach to a pod? or a frontdoor->proxy retry?

Elaine: frontdoor->proxy->upstream. sequence: client sends initial POST, frontdoor returns immediate 101 to start streaming, proxy opens connection to upstream. if upstream times out first attach, proxy retries the entire request. meanwhile upstream accepted the first and started side-effects.

Marcus: can you paste the simplified flow? a tiny ASCII helps.

Elaine: sure:
```
client -> frontdoor : POST /v1/stream
frontdoor -> client : 101 Switching Protocols (conn accepted)
frontdoor -> proxy : open connection
proxy -> upstream : POST /v1/stream (attempt #1)
(upstream slow, accepts later)\nproxy -> upstream : POST /v1/stream (attempt #2)
```
Result: upstream may receive 2 posts for same client request id.

Raj: oh that's rough. do we currently attach any idempotency token at gateway layer? x-request-id isn't sufficient for upstream dedupe.

Elaine: we include x-request-id but upstream models may not honor it. also for streaming calls we need the same socket context — dedupe at application-level is tricky.

Marcus: tradeoffs: 1) prevent proxy from retrying once we've issued 101. 2) make upstream dedupe robust using a signed idempotency key + short-lived lock. 3) change handshake so we only 101 after upstream attach success. each has perf/availability cost.

Raj: 1) seems simplest: once frontdoor returns early-ack, proxy must treat the request as in-flight and not retry. downside: what if the upstream connection truly failed and we want to failover to warm standby? we'd have to surface failure to client (close stream) rather than transparently retry.

Elaine: exactly. product may prefer transparent failover for reliability. but that risks duplicate processing.

Marcus: 2) upstream dedupe is safest functionally. signed idempotency key flow: gateway generates id_key = HMAC(key, x-request-id + client-ts) and passes id_key header. upstream tries to acquire short lock (redis or in-memory) keyed by id_key before side-effecting. if lock exists, it either resumes streaming or rejects duplicate. cost: extra distributed locking per request, potential latency.

Raj: we already have a short-lived request metadata store in infra for rate accounting. could extend to track in-flight streaming ids — maybe TTL 30s and a fast memcache. cheaper than cross-region locks.

Elaine: good point. only need single-region strong dedupe for Dedicated/Private; hosted multi-region is harder.

Marcus: 3) only 101 after upstream attach is most conservative: frontdoor buffers the client handshake until connection is established. that adds extra client latency and breaks our current fast-start UX.

Raj: another idea: mark retries as non-idempotent vs idempotent by header. e.g., x-retry-policy: allow-failover | no-retry-on-early-ack. frontdoor sets based on model config. then proxy enforces.

Elaine: we could default to allow-failover for non-actionable inference requests, but force no-retry-on-early-ack for any request that includes side-effect headers (x-side-effect: true) or is in a workspace with strict semantics.

Marcus: ok. propose next steps:
- add a short-lived in-flight cache prototype in proxy (memcache) keyed by hmac(id) — Raj to spike and measure latency.
- introduce x-retry-policy header semantics and config knobs in frontdoor — Elaine to draft API and default behavior.
- document UX impact for canary: change to default no-retry-on-early-ack for workspaces flagged as "strict-side-effects".

Raj: i'll spike the memcache write/read and simulate 99th percentile latencies. if overhead < 1ms median, i'm +1.

Elaine: i'll write the header spec and add config toggle in frontdoor (per-tenant). also add a test plan: create a fake upstream that accepts but delays processing and assert no duplicate side-effects.

SRE-bot: deploy-bot: canary request created: arch/proxy-halfopen-dedupe-spike -> staging, ETA 2d.

Marcus: thanks. one more edge case: streaming reconnects from client mid-session (client retries) — we should ensure id_key lifetime covers client reconnection window so reconnections are associated.

Raj: noted, will parameterize TTL and expose as config.

Elaine: cool. will sync with product about default behavior. i'll update this thread with the API draft later today. :thumbsup:
